_comment: Verified live 2026-07-11 (glassdoor.ca, jobs split-pane view). CRITICAL scoping rule: on the jobs page there is a left list of many job cards AND a right detail pane showing the currently-OPEN job. A global querySelector for a company/id class matches the FIRST left-list card, NOT the open job — this caused applications to be attributed to whichever job auto-opened on page load. The fix is that all selectors below target elements that exist ONLY in the detail pane: 'JobDetails_employerAndJobTitle' (the header block wrapping the open job's employer h4 + title h1) and the h1's own id 'jd-job-title-{listingId}'. Glassdoor uses CSS Modules (stable readable prefix, churning hash suffix), so '[class*="prefix"]' partial matches are the right tool. Do NOT reintroduce a bare '[class*="EmployerName"]' selector — that matches the left-list compact cards and reopens the wrong-job bug.
_locationModalityComment: Location verified live 2026-08-13 (glassdoor.ca detail pane): the location badge carries a stable 'data-test="location"' attribute, scoped by construction to the open job (it's nested under the same JobDetails_ detail-pane tree, never the left-list cards). Modality is UNVERIFIED — neither of two tested postings (one on-site, one from a 'remote' search) rendered a distinct workplace-type badge; the closest signal seen was prose inside the job description ('hybrid remote working environment'), which is too unreliable to scan (JD body text, not structured metadata) and is deliberately NOT matched here. modalityContainerSelectors targets the same badges wrapper location lives in, in case Glassdoor renders a workplace-type badge there for some postings — degrades to 'not detected' rather than false-matching JD prose if it doesn't. Needs a live check against a posting that actually has one.
